passages.text: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about food sacrificed to idols.
We all have knowledge about this matter.
Knowledge can make a person proud.
Love helps people grow and become stronger.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ

passages.text: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
passages.sermon:
A person may think he knows something.
He does not yet know as he should know.
He does not have true understanding.
He still lacks the knowledge he needs.
passages.original: εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἐγνωκέναι τι οὔπω ἔγνω καθὼς δεῖ γνῶναι

passages.text: But the one who loves God is known by God.
passages.sermon: God knows people who love Him.\r\nA person who loves God is recognized by God.\r\nGod sees and acknowledges those who love Him.
passages.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν Θεόν οὗτος ἔγνωσται ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about eating food sacrificed to idols.
Paul teaches that idols have no real existence in the world.
Paul says that only one God exists.
No other gods are real.
passages.original: Περὶ τῆς βρώσεως οὖν τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς Θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς

passages.text: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords), yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
passages.sermon:
Many people say there are gods in heaven.
Many people say there are gods on earth.
There are many so-called gods.
There are many so-called lords.
But for us, there is only one God.
He is the Father.
All things came from the Father.
We exist for the Father.
There is only one Lord.
He is Jesus Christ.
All things came through Jesus Christ.
We exist through Jesus Christ.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ εἴπερ εἰσὶν λεγόμενοι θεοὶ εἴτε ἐν οὐρανῷ εἴτε ἐπὶ γῆς ὥσπερ εἰσὶν θεοὶ πολλοὶ καὶ κύριοι πολλοί ἀλλ’ ἡμῖν εἷς Θεὸς ὁ Πατήρ ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν καὶ εἷς Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός δι’ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς δι’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
passages.sermon:
Not everyone knows that idols are nothing and that there is only one God.
Some people are still used to idols.
They eat food as if it is really sacrificed to an idol.
Their conscience is weak.
Their weak conscience becomes defiled.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις τινὲς δὲ τῇ συνηθείᾳ ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται

passages.text: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
passages.sermon:
Food does not bring us closer to God.
God does not accept us because of what we eat.
If we do not eat certain foods, we do not lose anything before God.
If we do eat, we do not gain anything before God.
passages.original: βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ παραστήσει τῷ Θεῷ οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν ὑστερούμεθα οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν περισσεύομεν

passages.text: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
passages.sermon:
You have freedom as a Christian.
Some believers are weak in conscience.
Be careful with your freedom.
Do not let your freedom cause weak believers to stumble.
passages.original: Βλέπετε δὲ μή πως ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη πρόσκομμα γένηται τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν

passages.text: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
passages.sermon:
A person may have a weak conscience.
You have knowledge about idols and food.
You eat in an idol’s temple.
The person with a weak conscience sees you eating there.
He sees that you have knowledge.
His conscience is weak.
He will be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols.
passages.original: ἐὰν γάρ τις ἴδῃ σὲ τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ κατακείμενον οὐχὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτοῦ ἀσθενοῦς ὄντος οἰκοδομηθήσεται εἰς τὸ τὰ εἰδωλόθυτα ἐσθίειν

passages.text: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
passages.sermon:
Christ died for your brother.
Your brother is weak.
Your knowledge causes harm.
Your knowledge destroys your weak brother.
passages.original: ἀπόλλυται γὰρ ὁ ἀσθενῶν ἐν τῇ σῇ γνώσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς δι’ ὃν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
passages.sermon: You sin against your brothers when you act in this way.\r\nYou hurt their weak conscience.\r\nWhen you do this, you sin against Christ.
passages.original: οὕτως δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τύπτοντες αὐτῶν τὴν συνείδησιν ἀσθενοῦσαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνετε

passages.text: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul cares about his fellow believers.
Paul knows that some believers are weak in conscience.
Paul says, “If my food causes my brother to stumble, I will not eat meat again.”
Paul does this to avoid causing his brother to stumble.
Paul chooses to give up his right to eat meat for the sake of his brother.
passages.original: Διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω
